verses.text: How miserable I am! I’m like someone gathering summer fruit after the harvest, gleaning what’s left in a vineyard. There’s no cluster of grapes to eat, though I crave an early fig.
Faithful people have disappeared from the land. No one upright is left. Everyone lies in wait to shed blood; each person hunts their own relative with a net.
Their hands are skilled at doing evil. The ruler and judge demand bribes; the powerful person gets whatever they desire. They conspire together.
Even the best among them is like a thornbush; the most upright is worse than a hedge of thorns. The day your watchmen warned about has come; now confusion is yours.
Don’t trust your neighbor or rely on a friend. Be careful what you say, even to the one lying in your arms.
A son dishonors his father; a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A person’s enemies are in their own household.
But I will look to the LORD. I will wait for the God who saves me. My God will hear me.
Don’t celebrate over me, my enemy! Though I fall, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
I will bear the LORD’s anger because I sinned against him, until he takes up my case and gives me justice. He will bring me out into the light, and I will see his righteousness.
Then my enemy will see it, and shame will cover her—the one who asked me, ‘Where is the LORD your God?’ My eyes will see her downfall; she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
The day is coming to rebuild your walls; that day will stretch out your borders.
On that day people will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
But the land will be desolate because of what its people have done.
Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock that belongs to you, living alone in the woods. Let them graze in fertile pastureland—in Bashan and Gilead, as in days long ago.
“As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them wonderful things.”
The nations will see and be embarrassed by all their strength. They will cover their mouths, and their ears will stop up.
They will lick the dust like a snake, crawl trembling out of their hiding places, and come fearfully to the LORD our God. They will be afraid of you.
Who is a God like you? You forgive guilt and pass over the rebellion of the remnant who belong to you. You don’t stay angry forever; you delight in faithful love.
You will again have compassion on us. You will trample our sins underfoot and throw all our sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and faithful love to Abraham, just as you promised our ancestors long ago.
